The Senior Staff Association of Statutory Corporations and Government-Owned Companies has commenced picketing of the headquarters of the Raw Materials Research and Development Council in Abuja over unresolved labour disputes and alleged violations of workers’ rights. The industrial action followed the expiration of a three-day notice issued to the council’s management after an earlier seven-working-day ultimatum, dated September 23, 2026, failed to resolve the grievances raised by the union. In a statement, the Acting General Secretary of SSASCGOC, Akin Okudero, accused the RMRDC management of failing to address several labour and administrative issues affecting senior officers of the council. The union alleged that management had failed to remit check-off dues deducted from members’ salaries, interfered in its internal operations and restricted the constitutional rights of eligible senior staff to freely join and participate in its activities. It also accused the management of refusing to recognise the SSASCGOC RMRDC branch executive and suppressing the activities of the branch and its general membership. SSASCGOC warned that the dispute could escalate into full-scale industrial action, including total and indefinite picketing of the council’s headquarters, if management failed to resolve the issues by November 11, 2026. The union said the action was intended to compel the council to address the outstanding labour issues and restore industrial harmony. The union warned that failure to address its demands before the expiration of the three-day notice on November 11 would trigger full industrial action. It said this would include total and indefinite picketing of the RMRDC headquarters in Abuja without further notice. SSASCGOC urged the council’s management to use the remaining window to address its demands and avert an industrial shutdown.
